subject.title: feat(subagents): native announceTarget for subagent completion routing (#27445)

question: Should native subagent completion routing become a supported per-spawn and persistent per-agent/global configuration contract, including parent-only delivery with no channel fallback?
rationale: The code can implement either policy safely, but repository guidance treats new config/default and message-delivery behavior as a product and compatibility choice that cannot be inferred from tests or contributor proof.

options.title: Sponsor a narrower per-spawn API
options.body: Accept parent-target routing as an explicit `sessions_spawn` choice while deferring persistent defaults until usage proves they are necessary.

options.title: Sponsor the full contract
options.body: Accept the per-spawn, per-agent, and global configuration surfaces with the documented no-channel-fallback semantics.

options.title: Keep channel delivery canonical
options.body: Decline the new routing contract and retain the existing channel-first completion policy and documented callback workarounds.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrower per-spawn API
recommendation.body: Accept parent-target routing as an explicit `sessions_spawn` choice while deferring persistent defaults until usage proves they are necessary.

likelyOwner.reason: The historical direct completion-delivery implementation and adjacent merge history make this person the strongest available owner for the permanent behavior contract.
